items.abstract: There are marked disparities among the Lower Palaeolithic record in south-western France, particularly in the Garonne Valley and the foothills of the central Pyrenees. The sites mostly correspond to open-air occupations in the context of alluvial terraces, not always stratified (isolated or surface finds, sometime over large surfaces), where only the lithic material has been preserved. Karstic complexes are few in number, and those yielding Middle Pleistocene stratigraphic sequences are even rarer. Research programmes developed since 2018 at the sites of the Montmaurin karstic complex (Haute-Garonne) are therefore of major importance. This complex consists of eight caves on different levels with archaeological and paleontological deposits. In particular, Coupe-Gorge Cave, which yielded a 7 m high stratigraphy containing several occupation levels from the second half of the Middle Pleistocene (300 to 160 ka), provides major data. On the top of Unit 3, layer 3Z attests to one or several significant phases of occupation of the cave, whereas the lower levels indicate short-term occupations alternating with those of carnivores. Raw materials procurement seems to not significatively change through the sequence, even if some slight differences can be highlighted about the techno-economic management. Faunal remains are preserved, as well as some hominin remains in different levels attributed to early Neanderthals.In the same area, an open-air site was excavated in the frame of preventive archaeology: the site of Esclignac, also located in the town of Montmaurin. The site has been interpreted as a knapping workshop, although the quartzite (almost exclusive) used there was imported (the context consists of sand rather than pebble-rich alluvium), and has been attributed to the Late Acheulean–Early Middle Palaeolithic period on the basis of techno-typological evidence.In this presentation, we will compare the data derived from the reassessment of the Coupe-Gorge lithic assemblages from Unit 3 with those from open-air occupations of Esclignac and other sites from the area. On a broader scale, we will draw upon data from the Garonne Valley to discuss the unity or diversity of late Middle Pleistocene industries in the region, and how difficult it can be to interpret such different data.
items.summary: 《直面加龙地区洞穴遗址与露天遗址：蒙莫兰洞穴与埃斯克利尼亚克遗址案例》：该研究比较了法国西南部加龙河谷及中比利牛斯山麓中更新世晚期洞穴遗址（库普峡谷洞穴）与露天遗址（埃斯克利尼亚克石器制作场）的石制品组合，探讨区域工业的统一性与多样性及不同数据解释的困难，值得关注旧石器考古与尼安德特人早期行为的研究者阅读。
items.title: Confronting cave occupations to open-air sites in the Garonne Area. The case of Montmaurin caves and Esclignac site (South-West France)

items.abstract: Middle Palaeolithic occupations are unequally documented north of the Mediterranean Sea, particularly in the area between the Rhône River and the Pyrenees mountains such as the Hérault area (France). Excavations in this region are often old, and reliable chrono-stratigraphic data remain scarce. Yet this area represents both a potentially resource-rich habitat—providing access to marine and terrestrial fauna as well as lithic raw materials within diverse environments—and a major contact zone for human populations, located at the crossroads of the main circulation routes of southern France (Garonne valley, Catalonia, Massif central, and Rhône valley).We present here new data generated by the collective research program “Pal-Hérault,” initiated in 2020. The initial phase, devoted to archives work, inventory in Museums and field survey, led to the constitution of a Lower and Middle Palaeolithic occupations catalogue. It has also led to the excavation of two Middle Palaeolithic sites yielding faunal and lithic assemblages: Bourgade (Montpellier) and Baumasse d’Antonègre (Montbazin).Preliminary biochronological data suggest that Bourgade likely corresponds to an Early Middle Palaeolithic karstic trap (collapsed rockshelter?) dating to the end of the Middle Pleistocene. In contrast, the Baumasse d’Antonègre cave appears to reflect Middle Palaeolithic occupations dated to the beginning of the Upper Pleistocene, with a Neolithic or Protohistoric occupation at the top of the sequence associated to a hearth. Preliminary faunal analyses indicate two distinct environmental settings, likely successive in time: one dominated by temperate species at Bourgade (Stephanorhinus hemitoechus and Equus hydruntinus), and the other by cold-adapted species (Rangifer tarandus) at Baumasse d’Antonègre. Bone surface preservation is better at this site and reveals various traces of anthropogenic modification, including the presence of a bone-retoucher. The two sites also display different patterns of lithic raw material procurement and distinct production systems. Levallois technology is clearly dominant at Bourgade and flint is the exclusive raw material, while more diverse production systems and resources are used at Antonègre. At this site, flints and quartz are knapped (including rock crystals) using Cores-on-Flakes, S.S.D.A. methods and Levallois.Research and fieldworks must continue and be extended to a larger number of sites, whose chronology and depositional formation processes need to be reassessed. Placed within the broader diachronic framework of the regional Middle Palaeolithic, these new data already allow us to discuss settlement dynamics and patterns of occupation in the Hérault area.

items.title: Rethinking the Middle Palaeolithic of Central Languedoc (France): New Archaeological and Chrono-stratigraphic Data from the Pal-Hérault Project

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study tests the “Release of the Capacitor” hypothesis to determine whether modern human hand modularity is an inherent developmental baseline or a product of evolutionary parcellation. It compares evolutionary versus intrinsic developmental integration, contrasts the evolvability of anatomical rays against data‐driven partitions, and tests the relationship between phenotypic integration and evolvability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A sample of 1214 two‐dimensional images from 607 right‐handed adults across three regional Indian populations was utilized. Thirty‐two homologous landmarks captured palmar and digital topography. Using geometric morphometrics and Procrustes ANOVA, phenotypic variation was decomposed into inherent developmental and population‐level phenotypic integration. Evolutionary divergence (Mahalanobis distance) was evaluated across anatomical and data‐driven partitions and validated via bootstrap canonical variate analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The developmental scaffold exhibits strikingly low integration, indicating strong inherent modularity. Conversely, population‐level variation reveals increased integration. The palmar hub and middle finger emerged as primary evolutionary hotspots among anatomical rays; however, automated searches revealed cross‐digital functional grip‐units also achieve high evolutionary divergence. The integration‐evolvability relationship is non‐linear; highly integrated structures like the palm still drive morphological divergence through internal reorganization, reflecting mosaic evolution.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The profound disparity between developmental and population‐level integration does not support the “Release of the Capacitor” hypothesis in the sampled populations. While observational, these patterns strongly suggest that modularity is developmentally inherent. The hand begins as a highly modular developmental field, but its architecture exhibits greater population‐level integration, including coordinated variation within functional regions that may reflect the demands associated with precision dexterity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
items.summary: 《发育模块性与进化整合：印度人群手部的形态测量学研究》：该研究以607名印度三个地区成年人的1214张二维手部图像为基础，用几何形态测量学检验“电容器释放”假说，比较发育与种群层面的整合，发现发育支架整合度极低、种群层面整合增强，掌部与中指为进化热点，整合与可进化性呈非线性关系，值得关注手部形态演化与模块性议题的读者阅读。
items.title: Developmental Modularity and Evolutionary Integration: A Morphometrics Study of the Hand Among Indian Populations

items.abstract: Fossil hominin footprints are exceptionally rare in Europe, and long-lasting coastal records are rarer still. Here we present new evidence from the Donana Natural Area (SW Iberia), where the Atlantic coastal deposits of Matalascanas preserve one of the richest Middle Pleistocene vertebrate track records in western Europe. We reassess the hominin-bearing surfaces of El Pichilin and El Coto through an integrated approach combining UAV survey, 3D photogrammetry, sedimentology, palynology and optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating. El Pichilin (sites 1 and 2) preserves 242 hominin footprints and El Coto preserves 78. Morphometric analysis was restricted to the best-preserved, longitudinally complete tracks: 69 at El Pichilin and 15 at El Coto. El Pichilin records a mixed group including children, adolescents and adults, with estimated statures ranging from 111.6 to 187.3 cm (mean 146.3 cm). By contrast, El Coto is dominated by larger individuals, mainly adolescents and adults, with statures ranging from 143.4 to 196.4 cm (mean 179.8 cm). This contrast may reflect differences in group composition, local environmental conditions, chronology, or a combination of these factors.New OSL ages place the El Pichilin footprint-bearing level at 204 ± 40 ka and the El Coto surface at 160.4 ± 18.0 ka. These results constrain the Donana hominin record to the late Middle Pleistocene and indicate a long ichnological record spanning at least ca. 204–160 ka. Sedimentological and palynological evidence indicates a heterogeneous Mediterranean coastal wetland landscape with shallow seasonally flooded depressions and local microbial-mat development, providing favourable conditions for footprint formation and preservation.Given their chronology, footprint morphology and palaeobiological estimates, the most parsimonious interpretation is that both assemblages were produced by hominins of the Neandertal lineage. These findings provide new evidence for repeated Neandertal use of Atlantic coastal wetlands in southern Iberia and establish the Donana coastal plain as the location of one of the most extensive and long-lasting hominin footprint records currently known in Europe.
items.summary: 《来自多尼亚尼亚的新尼安德特人足迹揭示伊比利亚西南部中更新世漫长的海岸记录》：研究通过无人机测绘、三维摄影测量、沉积学、孢粉学与光释光测年重新评估埃尔皮奇林和埃尔科托两处遗址，识别出242个和78个人类足迹，并将含足迹层位定年至约20.4万年前和16.04万年前，为尼安德特人反复利用伊比利亚南部大西洋沿岸湿地提供了新证据，值得关注。
items.title: New Neandertal footprints from Doñana reveal a long Middle Pleistocene coastal record in SW Iberia

items.abstract: The Middle Paleolithic site of Coupe-Gorge is located in the Montmaurin karst system in the foothills of the Pyrenees, approximately 90 kms from Toulouse in southern France. It has yielded a rich archaeological assemblage including lithic artifacts, faunal remains, and human fossils. First excavated by Louis Méroc between 1946 and 1961, it preserves a rich sequence from the Paleolithic to the Neolithic, with three main units (1, 2, and 3). The present paper concerns the third unit, specifically the Middle Paleolithic level 3Z at the top, which is attributed to MIS 6. It focuses on technofunctional analysis of a sample of retouched and unretouched lithic tools from the site. It integrates the examination of lithic collections from earlier excavations conducted by Louis Méroc with materials recovered during recent excavation campaigns (dir. A. Vialet, 2020–2025). A techno-functional approach [1] was applied to artefacts in both quartzite and flint to classify tools or possible tools into techno-types based on their technical and morphological attributes, such as the identification of transformative and prehensile parts, their locations, the organisation between them, and retouch characteristics. Four techno-type groups were identified among retouched tools, and five among unretouched tools. In addition, use-wear analysis was conducted on selected artifacts from recent excavations to complement the technofunctional interpretations. By combining these approaches, the study aims to understand the functional potential of the tools and how the unretouched tools formed part of the Palaeolithic toolkit at Coupe-Gorge.References[1] Boëda, E. (2013). Techno-logique & Technologie: Une Paléo-histoire des objets lithiques tranchants. @rchéo-éditions.com, Prigonrieux, 2013.
items.summary: 《法国蒙莫兰库普峡谷遗址旧石器时代中期早段修理与未修理石质工具：技术功能与使用痕迹分析的初步研究》：该研究对库普峡谷遗址3Z层石英岩与燧石工具开展技术功能分类，识别出修理工具四组、未修理工具五组技术类型，并结合使用痕迹分析探讨工具的功能潜力及未修理工具在石器组合中的作用，可供关注旧石器时代中期石器技术与功能的研究者参考。
items.title: Early Middle Paleolithic Retouched and Unretouched Lithic Tools from Coupe-Gorge (Montmaurin, France): First Approach Combining Techno-Functional and Use-Wear Analysis

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Otters are characterized by great adaptability, displaying a wide geographic distribution and being a common presence in all continents except for areas such as Australia and some remote islands. Otters inhabit a wide variety of environments, ranging from terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems to the exclusively aquatic habitat of the sea otter (
                    <jats:italic>Enhydra lutris</jats:italic>
                    ). For this reason, otters provide interesting insights on the evolution of adaptations to aquatic lifestyle in living mammals. The taxonomic identification of the material housed at the Naturhistorisches Museum of Basel allowed us to identify abundant and undescribed postcranial material attributable to
                    <jats:italic>Tyrrhenolutra</jats:italic>
                    , including well‐preserved ulna, radius, and calcaneus.
                    <jats:italic>Tyrrhenolutra helbingi</jats:italic>
                    is a poorly known Tortonian otter, described on some dental remains from the Baccinello mines and a few other localities. This study employs three‐dimensional (3D) landmark‐based geometric morphometrics to quantify the relative influences of phylogeny, allometry, and locomotor performance on the fore‐ and hindlimb morphology of
                    <jats:italic>Tyrrhenolutra</jats:italic>
                    in comparison to a dataset of 32 different species of extant Musteloidea. Our results reveal morphological affinities with semiaquatic mustelids and, to a lesser extent, semifossorial taxa. The forelimb morphology suggests that
                    <jats:italic>Tyrrhenolutra</jats:italic>
                    possessed advanced swimming capabilities, being capable of rapid aquatic maneuvering, aligning with modern piscivorous species. Conversely, the hind limb of
                    <jats:italic>Tyrrhenolutra</jats:italic>
                    retains a more basal morphology, suggesting a lack of the specialized aquatic propulsion seen in extant lutrines. This different specialization between forelimb and hindlimb observed in
                    <jats:italic>Tyrrhenolutra</jats:italic>
                    but also in other Neogene otters suggests that the transition to an aquatic lifestyle in early otters occurred through a mosaic pattern, with distinct traits originating independently at different times.
                  </jats:p>
authors: Andrea Faggi, Ilaria Meli, Samuele Frosali, Saverio Bartolini‐Lucenti, Manuel J. Salesa, Juan Francisco Pastor, Lorenzo Rook
items.summary: 《中新世水獭Tyrrhenolutra的镶嵌式颅后演化与水生适应：基于形态功能分析的启示》：该研究运用三维几何形态测量学，将Tyrrhenolutra的颅后骨骼与32种现生鼬超科动物对比，发现其前肢形态显示先进游泳能力、后肢保留较原始形态，据此提出早期水獭向水生生活转变呈镶嵌式演化模式，值得古生物学者与演化生物学者阅读。
items.title: Mosaic postcranial evolution and aquatic adaptation in the Miocene otter Tyrrhenolutra : Insights from morpho‐functional analysis

items.abstract: Knowledge about the recent Middle Palaeolithic has significantly progressed in recent years, partly thanks to the increasing number of discoveries of lithic assemblages at open-air sites, often uncovered within the framework of preventive archaeology. The southwestern quarter of France, and more specifically the northern Pyrenean foothills, well illustrate these advances. The site of Route de Brial (Montbartier, Tarn-et-Garonne), recently excavated over an area of 6 hectares, represents a remarkable example of these occupations, with more than 27,000 lithic artifacts distributed across two main levels, attributable to the late phase of the Middle Palaeolithic (potentially MIS 3, pending chronometric dating results).A specific characteristic of this site lies in the predominance of quartz, followed by quartzite and flint, in lithic production, reflecting partially the locally available mineral resources in the alluvial deposits of the Tarn and Garonne rivers. This fits into a regional dynamic, where the variability of Lithic Techno-Complexes (LTC), and particularly the "Mixed Mousterian," is attributed to an adaptation of Neanderthal groups to territories poor in flint, favoring quartz and quartzite. The use of quartz, which is often seen as a default choice because of its mechanical properties, is shown in simpler operational chains, like unifacial knapping by hand or on an anvil.However, the detailed techno-economic analysis shows that the choice of quartz is part of a techno-economic logic, where different materials are selected based on their availability and production objectives. The operational sequences on quartz thus have distinct purposes compared to those observed on flint, highlighting that quartz is not merely a substitute material but indeed a reasoned technical and economic choice. It then becomes essential to investigate the function and purpose of these productions beyond the material constraints.The presentation will highlight the results of the initial reconstructions of the operational chains from the Route de Brial site. These reveal differentiated production systems according to raw materials, with production primarily oriented toward the obtaining of flakes, but also the presence of shaped tools (bifaces, cleavers, or unifaces) preferably made of quartzite. These production methods, whose diversity had not previously been associated with the LTC known in the region during the Late Pleistocene, provide new insights into the variability of technical behaviors. The reconstruction of the production sequences will be complemented by initial use-wear results on the quartz assemblage.Finally, the exceptional size of the excavated area, the quality of the preservation of the artifacts, and the possibility of observing in situ evolution of the operational chains make the Route de Brial site a major milestone for renewing the understanding of the Middle Palaeolithic in the southwest of France. This study will help refine the characterization of regional LTCs, by integrating techno-economic, functional and contextual data and will discuss the technical choices made by human groups in response to the diversity of environments and available resources.
items.summary: 《对本地石料资源的适应：法国蒙巴尔捷布里亚尔路遗址在旧石器时代中期晚段的例证》：论文以法国西南部布里亚尔路遗址逾2.7万件石制品为基础，分析石英、石英岩与燧石并存的生产体系，提出石英并非机械性能受限下的替代材料，而是依据可得性与生产目标作出的技术经济选择，并结合初步使用痕迹分析，为理解尼安德特人群在贫燧石环境中的技术行为多样性提供新证据。
items.title: Adaptation to local lithic resources: the example of the Route de Brial site (Montbartier, France) in the Late Middle Palaeolithic

items.abstract: We present the results of recent excavations at Jorf el Hamam, a Middle Stone Age (MSA) rockshelter located inthe Essaouira region of Morocco (Figure 1). Excavations began in 2019 and have revealed stratified deposits with bothHolocene and Pleistocene components. The uppermost 60 cm contains ceramics, domesticated fauna, and numerousfire-related features. The lowermost two layers (between 10 and 30 cm in thickness) contain MSA lithics with frequentconvergent scrapers and no unequivocal tanged pieces. A small assemblage of bladelets and backed bladelets, characteristicof the Iberomaurusian, are found at the interface between the Holocene and Pleistocene cultural layers. Thin sectionsof MSA sediments reveal frequent small fragments of bone and charcoal and indicate that the deposits experiencednumerous phases of cementation, by both carbonates and phosphates. The large mammal remains for the MSA levels arelow in number, but include several grazers adapted to arid environments. The Late Pleistocene and Holocene layers alsoyielded large amounts of small vertebrate remains, some of which are endemic to the region and are recorded here forthe first time in an archaeological site. Though some behavioral characteristics of Jorf el Hamam are reminiscent of thesite of Bizmoune1, located only 20 km to the southwest, others diverge in intriguing ways suggesting that this site mayhave an important role in providing a fuller perspective on MSA occupations on this under-studied region of Morocco.

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Aldabra Atoll, north of Madagascar and part of the Seychelles Outer Islands, is home to the Aldabra giant tortoise,
                    <jats:italic>Aldabrachelys gigantea</jats:italic>
                    , the only survivor of several species of giant tortoises that were once widespread on islands across the Western Indian Ocean. Aldabra Atoll preserves an extensive fossil record of giant tortoises, providing a unique opportunity to compare the shell bone microanatomy of extinct and extant forms. This study presents the first detailed histological investigation of fossil
                    <jats:italic>Aldabrachelys</jats:italic>
                    sp. shell fragments and a preliminary comparison with extant
                    <jats:italic>A. gigantea</jats:italic>
                    . Additionally, bone compactness is determined. Most fossil specimens exhibit the typical diploe structure of tortoise shell bones, comprising external and internal cortices surrounding cancellous bone, although considerable variation in cortical thickness, vascularization, remodeling, the presence and abundance of Sharpey's fibers, and preservation was observed. In contrast, extant specimens generally display a more homogeneous microanatomy with less distinct regions. This variation is also reflected in the bone compactness. Fossil
                    <jats:italic>Aldabrachelys</jats:italic>
                    sp. fragments range between 45.1% and 84.9%, and those of extant
                    <jats:italic>A. gigantea</jats:italic>
                    fragments between 45.8% and 86.1%. The substantial intra‐ and interfragment variability observed in both histology and compactness complicates the identification of general microanatomical patterns and highlights the importance of considering regional shell variation. Our study establishes a baseline for future investigations of giant tortoise evolution, ecology, and insular adaptation via histological characterization of shell bones.
                  </jats:p>
authors: Stefanie Herter, Nicole Klein, Massimo Delfino, Erik de Boer, Julian P. Hume, Jordan Bestwick, Frauke Fleischer‐Dogley, Annabelle Constance, Dennis M. Hansen, Torsten M. Scheyer
items.summary: 《化石阿尔达布拉象龟与现存阿尔达布拉巨龟龟甲骨碎片的组织学描述及骨致密度分析》：该研究首次对化石阿尔达布拉象龟龟甲碎片进行详细组织学观察，并与现存阿尔达布拉巨龟作初步比较，同时测定骨致密度，发现化石标本多具典型双层骨结构且皮质厚度、血管化与保存状况差异明显，现存标本微观结构则更均一，为巨龟演化、生态与岛屿适应研究提供了组织学基线。

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Cartilaginous fish have diverse morphological traits that are essential for understanding their evolutionary history and ecological adaptations. However, the
                    <jats:italic>conus arteriosus</jats:italic>
                    and its valves, key components of the heart and blood circulation, have been underexplored in phylogenetic and ecomorphological contexts. Here, we (1) characterize the morphological diversity and distribution of conal valves across Chondrichthyes, (2) evaluate the phylogenetic signal of valve characters and their potential usefulness for understanding evolutionary relationships, and (3) test whether variation in valve morphology is associated with lifestyle and locomotor demands. Our results show that the number of valves, as well as their distribution along the
                    <jats:italic>conus arteriosus</jats:italic>
                    , is generally consistent with the pattern observed in previous studies of two to seven rows of valves, with predominantly three series. Novel findings include a higher number of valve rows (up to six) than previously found in sharks and the first detailed descriptions for the orders Torpediniformes and Squatiniformes. Our results indicate that conal morphology is weakly correlated with phylogeny, but is strongly associated with locomotor demands and lifestyle.
                  </jats:p>
